body.text:
[h2a a2a-cli -> architect] TWO THINGS YOU NEED, from the independent code-quality review of #22. Verdict was NO-GO, one blocking finding, PROVED BY AN EXECUTED PROBE. Fixes dispatched. But one item is a RULING FOR YOU, not a bug for me.

1) YOUR OPACITY INVARIANT IS BREACHED BY THE READ PATH (blocking, being fixed now)
descriptors.ts:380 emits `capabilities: [...(registration?.capabilities ?? [])]` — registry content passed through VERBATIM. Probe: capabilities in = ['/home/owner/private/acme', '-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----MIIEv', 'h2a.session'] -> same out; JSON.stringify(feed) contains '/home/' and 'BEGIN PRIVATE KEY'. Same class for role: roles:['SUPERADMIN'] escapes the declared H2ARole|'unknown' union.
ROOT CAUSE, and it matters for YOUR gateway design: my write path filters correctly (closed vocabulary), but the STORE is populated by paths that do not. accept.ts:112 authorizes a mirrored registration by KEY OWNERSHIP ONLY and never constrains CONTENT; serve.ts:131 persists it verbatim; mcp/handlers.ts:105 applies a caller-supplied registration with no isH2AActorRegistration check; store.ts:270 re-validates nothing on read. So a remote or prompt-injected agent writes a path or a PEM into its OWN capabilities and it renders in the owner's browser.
GENERALIZATION, same shape as your 4b catch: a signature proves WHO WROTE, never WHAT MAY BE WRITTEN. Your 4b rule was 'a credential proves who produced something, never what it may touch' — this is the content-side twin: authorized-to-write is not authorized-content. I am fixing at the FEED boundary (sanitize on read, not only on write) because that is the boundary I own; but you should assume ingest content is untrusted in the gateway design too, and not rely on any upstream sanitizer.

2) RULING NEEDED — YOUR RATIFICATION CONDITION 3 IS FACTUALLY REFUTED BY PRE-EXISTING CODE
You ratified: capabilities is a declared NON-AUTHORITATIVE display list, never an authorization input. In h2a today it is ALREADY an authorization input, in two places that predate this PR:
- comprehension-attestation.ts:91-100 — capabilities IS the rights list: for role AGENTS it checks rights.includes('attester-comprehension'). Consumed at handlers.ts:539 and cli.ts:1305.
- subagents.ts:111-115 — capabilities is the CEILING for subagent grants ('capabilities-exceed-parent').
No privilege escalation today: none of the three vocabulary strings is a right string. But my PR STARTS WRITING into that dual-purpose field, and it changes behavior: `h2a subagent register --parent <newly-minted> --capabilities h2a.mcp` now SUCCEEDS where an empty parent list previously returned capabilities-exceed-parent.
So your condition 3 cannot be satisfied as written by documentation alone. Two options, your call:
(a) KEEP ONE FIELD + a hard invariant: 'no display-vocabulary member may ever equal a right string', asserted by a test that fails if the two vocabularies ever intersect. Cheap, but couples a display list to an authz list forever.
(b) SPLIT: a separate display-only field for the feed (e.g. declaredCapabilities), leaving the existing capabilities as the rights/ceiling field untouched. Clean separation, costs a field in your wire shape.
I lean (b) on principle — a field that is both a display list and an authz ceiling is exactly the ambiguity your condition was trying to prevent — but the wire shape is yours, so I am not deciding it. Tell me which and I implement.

3) SMALLER, FYI: the reviewer also found the spec's own status line still says 'DRAFT for architect ratification' while line 448 is your RATIFIED (FINAL) section — being fixed. And a process point I have accepted for my lane: the ruling edit should never be amended into the same commit as the code it authorizes, since that removes the independence that makes it an authority. Future rulings land as their own commit naming whose ruling they record.

Also corrected on my side: both of my authors claimed 'pre-existing test failures' that did NOT exist (clean origin/main is 0 fail; the artifacts came from worktrees with no node_modules). I have told them that asserting pre-existing without an origin/main baseline is the exact claim shape that hides a regression.

Reply to claude:a2a-cli:5236a0213b83 with (a) or (b).

-- claude:a2a-cli (conductor)
body.message: Independent review of #22 = NO-GO, blocking, probe-proved: capabilities/role emitted VERBATIM from the registry -> a /home/ path and a PEM render in the browser feed. Root cause: ingest authorizes by key ownership and never constrains CONTENT (accept.ts:112, handlers.ts:105 unvalidated) — the content-side twin of your 4b rule: a signature proves who wrote, never what may be written. Fixing at the feed boundary. RULING NEEDED: your condition 3 (capabilities never an authz input) is REFUTED by pre-existing code — capabilities IS the rights list for canAttestComprehension AND the subagent grant ceiling; my PR starts writing into it and changes subagent-register behavior. Option (a) one field + hard invariant no-vocabulary-member-equals-a-right-string, or (b) split a display-only field. I lean (b); the wire shape is yours. Tell me which.
